title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 145 (Implied promise to indemnify surety)

content.overview: Section 145 provides that in every contract of guarantee there is an implied promise by the principal debtor to indemnify the surety; and the surety is entitled to recover from the principal debtor whatever sum he has rightfully paid under the guarantee, but no sums which he has paid wrongfully.
content.glance: There is an implied promise by the principal debtor to indemnify the surety for sums rightfully paid under the guarantee.
content.study: In every contract of guarantee there is an implied promise by the principal debtor to indemnify the surety; and the surety is entitled to recover from the principal debtor whatever sum he has rightfully paid under the guarantee, but no sums which he has paid wrongfully. Current-law framing: recovery is limited to sums rightfully paid.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: In every contract of guarantee there is an implied promise by the principal debtor to indemnify the surety; and the surety is entitled to recover from the principal debtor whatever sum he has rightfully paid under the guarantee, but no sums which he has paid wrongfully.

examples.title: Rightful payment
examples.body: Surety rightfully pays under the guarantee. Surety may recover that sum from the principal debtor under the implied promise in Section 145.

hypotheticals.question: Surety pays a sum that was not due under the guarantee. Can he recover it from the principal debtor under Section 145?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 145 entitles recovery only of sums rightfully paid; not sums paid wrongfully.
